---
title: Look up items by title
description: Turn the names a person typed, such as the targets of links in their notes, into the items those names title, many names in one request.
---

A person names items by their titles, as in a link written `[[Reading list]]`. To turn such names into items, send up to 200 of them in one request, and Marfa answers each one. In the TypeScript example, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows.

## Look up names

[Find items by title](/api-reference/items/findItemsByTitle) takes the names and answers each one:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items titles "Reading list" Plans
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items/titles
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "names": ["Reading list", "Plans"] }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.POST("/items/titles", {
  body: { names: ["Reading list", "Plans"] },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "data": [
    { "name": "Reading list", "items": [], "more": false },
    {
      "name": "Plans",
      "items": [
        { "id": "01a1f124-f3e2-73e2-8bc4-78da7df78619", "type": "core.bookmark", "title": "Plans", "has_blob": false },
        { "id": "01a1f124-f44b-749f-b7a8-e1796f1dcfc4", "type": "core.collection", "title": "plans", "has_blob": false }
      ],
      "more": false
    }
  ]
}
```

**Each name gets one entry in `data`, in the order you sent them**, with the name as you sent it. A name that titles nothing gets no items, as `Reading list` does here. A name that titles several items gets them all, here a bookmark and a collection, so the person can choose. `has_blob` says whether the item holds a file.

## How a name matches

- **The whole title must match.** Case, the Unicode form and blank characters at either end don't count, so `Plans` finds `plans` and `  PLANS ` finds both. A name never matches part of a title, and a blank name matches nothing.
- **The title is the property the item's type is titled by**: the nearest `display_hints.title_field` up its type's parents, or `title` where none names one.
- **Only items the key can list count**, active or archived. Items in the bin, `system.*` items and items of a type the key can't read are left out, so a lookup never tells a key about an item it couldn't list.
- **A name that matches more than 20 items** answers the first 20 by `id`, with `more` set to `true`. Treat that name as naming no one item.
- **A title longer than 1,000 characters** matches no name.

## When a lookup is refused

- **More than 200 names, a name longer than 1,000 characters, or `names` that isn't a list of strings** answers `400 validation_error`.
- **A key that reaches no type** answers `403 type_not_permitted`.

A [synced folder](/use/sync-a-folder) looks up its links' names this way, and says so when the instance refuses: [links by name wait](/use/fix-a-folder#links-by-name-wait-since-the-server-has-no-title-lookup).

The rules behind this guide are under [`items/titles`](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md#itemstitles) in the contract.
